The native engine guide

Source: vignettes/articles/native-guide.qmd

The native engine fits models from lavaan-style syntax by maximum likelihood, with a covariance structure and, when you write intercepts, observed means. This guide covers the whole workflow in one place: syntax, fitting, inference, constraints, model comparison, diagnostics and the route to the mediation objects. It is experimental. For a first look, read the five-minute quickstart.

Entry points fit_sem(syntax, data); fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native") for one mediator
Class returned SEMFit, then MediationData, SerialMediationData or ParallelMediationData from extract_mediation()
Syntax reference ?"medfit-syntax"
Not covered latent means, latent products, groups, categorical outcomes, other estimators; see the limits 
library(medfit)

Attaching package: 'medfit'
The following object is masked from 'package:stats':

    decompose
library(generics)

Attaching package: 'generics'
The following objects are masked from 'package:base':

    as.difftime, as.factor, as.ordered, intersect, is.element, setdiff,
    setequal, union
d <- mediation_demo

1. Syntax

Statement Meaning
y ~ x1 + x2 regression of y on x1 and x2
f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 latent variable f measured by indicators
y1 ~~ y2 covariance; y1 ~~ y1 is a variance
y ~ a*x label a path; equal labels are one parameter
y ~ 0.5*x fix a path
start(0.3)*, lower(0)*, upper(1)* starting value, lower and upper bound
ab := a*b defined parameter with a delta-method standard error
a == b, cp == a*b, a*b > 0.1 equality or inequality constraint on labels, linear or not
y1, y2 ~ x comma shorthand (a medfit extension; lavaan reads it differently)

Exogenous variables get free variances and covariances, as lavaan does with fixed.x = FALSE; fixed_x = TRUE in fit_sem() fixes them at the sample moments instead (fewer parameters, the same structural estimates, a conditional log likelihood). Both sides of a constraint and the right side of a definition are arithmetic expressions in the labels (+ - * / ^, parentheses, exp, log, sqrt, abs, min, max, pnorm, qnorm, and a few more).

2. Fit and read 

syntax <- "
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment + covariate1
  ab := a * b
  total := cp + a * b
"
fit <- fit_sem(syntax, d)
summary(fit)

The chi-square is \(n\) times the minimized discrepancy and has df degrees of freedom. A saturated model (here df = 0) fits perfectly by construction, so the test only means something when there are restrictions.

3. Standard errors and weights

The default information matrix is observed; information = "expected" gives lavaan’s default. se_type = "sandwich" gives the HC0 robust covariance, and weights takes case weights.

w <- seq_len(nrow(d)) %% 3 + 1
robust <- fit_sem(syntax, d, weights = w, se_type = "sandwich")
rbind(model_based = sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))[1:3], weighted_robust = sqrt(diag(vcov(robust)))[1:3])
                         a mediator1~covariate1          b
model_based     0.09858458           0.04833820 0.05306479
weighted_robust 0.10207525           0.04774111 0.06498487

4. Constraints

A constraint is a line of syntax. The engine classifies it and uses the cheapest exact route:

Constraint Example How it is solved
linear equality or bound a == b, a + b == 1, a < 0.3 constant Jacobian rows; every accepted solution passes a gate on all rows
nonlinear equality cp == a*b Jacobian recomputed at every point; every start tried, the best accepted one kept; a Newton polish after acceptance
nonlinear inequality a*b > 0.1, ab > 0 with ab := a*b same, as rows \(c(\theta) \le 0\); a warning when the starts disagree
product set to zero a*b == 0, b1*b2*b3 == 0 exact: one linear fit per factor, smallest discrepancy kept
sum of products a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0 best-effort: the best of the starts; a disagreement warning means a better optimum may exist, so raise n_starts 
tied <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "cp == a * b\n"), d)
round(coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")], 4)
     a      b     cp
0.5423 0.5497 0.2981 
tied@diagnostics$active_constraints
[1] "cp == a * b"

Labels used in a constraint must be defined in the model, and a constraint with no free parameter is an error. CONSTRAINT(a == b) is the same as the bare a == b.

5. Compare models and test the indirect effect

anova() is the likelihood-ratio test for nested SEMFits; it refits nothing. Nesting is checked by parameter-table inclusion, a necessary condition, so two models that pass but are not nested in substance are your responsibility. mbco_sem() tests an indirect effect that is a product of paths:

anova(tied, fit)
Likelihood-ratio (chi-square difference) test for SEMFit models

n = 400; Chisq is n times the minimized discrepancy

     Df Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fit   0 0.000
tied  1 0.938    0.93802       1     0.3328
mbco_sem(fit, "a", "b")

    Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect

data:  a * b = 0
MBCO = 33.353, df = 1, p-value = 7.685e-09

For a chain a, d, b, give the paths: mbco_sem(fit, paths = c("a", "d", "b")) is the minimum of the single-path tests against a chi-square with one degree of freedom. The null is a union of hypotheses, so the test is conservative when more than one path is zero (its size is at most 0.055 at the 5% level in the package’s simulation gate).

6. Diagnostics

Read these before trusting a fit; all are in summary(fit) and fit@diagnostics:

Field What it says If it is wrong
Converged the optimizer returned and the acceptance gate passed the fit is not returned; the error names the failure
Optimizer status, stationarity the solver’s code and the Newton decrement at the solution a large decrement means a stall; try n_starts
Active bounds / Active constraints which bounds or constraints bind a binding bound means the estimate is on the edge
Improper solution a negative variance or non-positive definite covariance respecify, or bound the variance
Multiplier sign check active inequality multipliers have the right sign a wrong sign means an active bound was not optimal 
b <- fit_sem(paste0(syntax, "outcome ~~ lower(2) * outcome\n"), d)
b@diagnostics$active_bounds
[1] "outcome~~outcome"

When a model with a nonlinear constraint warns that the starts reached different optima, the constraint has more than one solution (a*b > 0.1 holds for two positive or two negative paths). The kept fit is the best, but say so in a report.

7. From a fit to mediation objects 

x <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       outcome = "outcome")
class(x)[1]
[1] "medfit::MediationData"

fit_mediation(model = syntax, engine = "native", treatment =, mediator =) does both steps for one mediator. For several mediators, fit with fit_sem() and call extract_mediation(fit, mediator = c("m1", "m2"), outcome = ): a chain gives a SerialMediationData, mediators side by side a ParallelMediationData. A latent mediator works through the same call.

Limits

  • Observed means only. Intercepts (y ~ 1, y ~ 1 + x) are estimated for observed variables; a free latent mean or intercept stops with “latent means are planned for a later release”.
  • One group, listwise deletion for missing data, numeric variables only.
  • ML only, plus the HC0 sandwich; no robust chi-square, no fit indices beyond the chi-square, AIC and BIC.
  • Products (x:m, which give the four-way decomposition) work for two observed variables inside a supported class; the table of limits and messages is on the native model page. The model test is NA when a product factor is a regression target.
  • AIC and BIC of a fit with a product are not comparable with those of a fit without one (the product column enters the likelihood), so AIC(fit_a, fit_b) and BIC() refuse such a pair; see the native model page.
  • For latent means, groups, categorical outcomes or fit indices use lavaan; the extraction route accepts a lavaan fit as well. See lavaan and the native engine.
